key_insight: TrajectoryFlowNet learns both how particles move over long distances and how the surrounding fluid flows from very limited trajectory measurements. It connects particle-following (Lagrangian) and fixed-location (Eulerian) descriptions through physics-informed learning.
problem_solved: Reconstructing fluid motion from sparse particle tracks is challenging, especially when both long-range trajectories and the underlying flow field must be predicted.
method: Use limited trajectory measurements to learn particle motion and the surrounding flow field together.
Incorporate physical constraints to connect Lagrangian trajectories with Eulerian flow predictions.
Validate the approach in simulations and blood-flow experiments.
impact: The work illustrates how physics-informed AI can extract richer predictions from scarce measurements. It offers a promising approach for practitioners working on fluid reconstruction, scientific machine learning and biomedical flow analysis.
visual_elements: Sparse measured particle tracks transitioning into extended predicted trajectories.
A split-panel diagram contrasting particle-following and fixed-location views of the same flow.
A model schematic linking trajectory measurements, physical constraints and joint predictions.
Side-by-side illustrations of simulation and blood-flow validation settings.
paper_title: Lagrangian–Eulerian learning of flow field and trajectories with TrajectoryFlowNet
paper_authors: Jingdi Wan, Hongping Wang, Bo Liu, Xiaolei Yang, Xiaodong Hu
